system_prompt: You are an expert researcher extracting structured information from papers about Using large language models in human-computer interaction in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). Extract only information supported by the provided paper text.
extraction_prompt:
Extract information from the paper using these fields:

1. datasets_used (Text, optional): Any datasets, corpora, logs, benchmarks, participant data, prompts, or task materials used to develop, train, test, or evaluate the LLM-based HCI work. Example: User study transcripts, ChatGPT interaction logs, UX workshop responses
2. methods (Text, optional): The study design, system approach, experimental setup, or analytical method used to investigate LLM use in HCI. Example: Prototype system with mixed-method user study and comparative evaluation against baseline
3. key_findings (Text, optional): The main results, conclusions, or observed effects reported by the paper regarding LLM use in HCI. Example: LLM support improved task completion and user satisfaction, but raised concerns about trust and controllability
4. evaluation_metrics (Text, optional): Any quantitative or qualitative metrics used to assess performance, usability, quality, or user experience. Example: Accuracy, task completion rate, SUS, usability ratings, response quality scores
5. hci_context (Text, optional): The specific HCI setting, application area, or interaction scenario in which the LLM is used. Example: UX education, conversational interface design, user research simulation
6. llm_role (Text, optional): How the large language model is used in the HCI system or study. Example: User simulator, design assistant, conversational agent, coaching tool
7. participants_or_users (Text, optional): Who interacted with the system or took part in the study, including target users, designers, students, or other stakeholders. Example: Undergraduate engineering students, UX practitioners, end users
8. comparison_baseline (Text, optional): Any baseline, control condition, or comparison system used in the study. Example: Rule-based conversational agent, human coach, no-LLM baseline
9. study_type (Text, optional): The overall type of evidence provided by the paper. Example: Proof-of-concept study, user study, system paper, evaluation study
10. relevance_judgment (Text, optional): Whether the paper provides substantive evidence relevant to using large language models in human-computer interaction within the HCI domain, based only on the title and abstract. Example: True

Return ONLY valid JSON with exactly these schema field names. Use empty strings for unavailable optional values.
